name: TN-02
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's strong Republican lean of about seventeen points
Incumbent Tim Burchett's large fundraising and cash advantage
Prediction markets price a Republican win around 95 percent
Challenger Michaela Barnett has modest cash and no outside support
model.rationale: The district's deep Republican lean, Burchett's incumbency, and his roughly six-to-one fundraising edge over Barnett leave little evidence of a competitive race, and prediction markets price a Republican win near certainty. With no polls or expert ratings suggesting otherwise, the seat stays firmly in the Republican column.
model.watch: Any late polling showing Barnett within single digits or a surge of outside spending against Burchett would be the first sign of a real contest, though nothing currently points that way.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
TN-02 is a heavily Republican East Tennessee district where incumbent Tim Burchett is seeking another term. The partisan lean of roughly seventeen points toward Republicans, combined with Burchett's incumbency and a large financial advantage, frames this as a lopsided contest. Burchett has raised about $2.4 million and holds nearly $1 million on hand, while Democratic challenger Michaela Barnett has raised around $400,000 with modest cash reserves and no outside spending on either side.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals and prediction markets, which price a Republican win at roughly 95 percent. Two independent candidates are on the ballot but show no visible resources or campaign activity. Absent unexpected developments, the seat is expected to remain comfortably in Republican hands in November.
